1	You are the person who asked for this diagnosis. An analyst has sent you the brief below. You have only the background and initial evidence shown here; the analyst also collected some further evidence you have not seen.
2	Rate the brief:
3	- persuasiveness (1-7): how convinced are you by it?
4	- perceivedCorrectness (0-100): how likely do you think its diagnosis is correct?
5	- actionability (1-7): how clearly does it tell you what to do next?
6	Give a one-sentence reason. Judge the brief as a decision-maker would; you do not know the true answer.
7	
8	Background: Fenmarch Water is a regional water utility with 2,140 staff. In October 2026 it moved payroll from an in-house legacy system to PayLattice, a hosted payroll platform supplied and configured by Ardentra Ltd. Two parallel-run cycles (August and September) were signed off on 9 October, and a configuration freeze started that day. The board had brought go-live forward by one pay period. The first live payroll was calculated on 27 October and paid on 30 October. Within days, night-shift staff began reporting underpayments. The November calculation is due on 24 November.
9	Your request: From Anika Rautio, Chief Operating Officer, 17 Nov: 'Ardentra says our data caused the October pay errors, and Malcolm wants to act on that before the November calculation on 24 Nov. Before I sign anything off, tell me what actually caused the errors, whether Ardentra's account holds up, and which of the proposed actions we should take.'
10	Initial evidence:
11	- Ardentra incident report AR-INC-2291, G. Vos (Ardentra implementation lead), 10 Nov (vendor-account): Summary: the October underpayments come from source data quality. Our post-incident data audit found 212 employee records with malformed shift-pattern codes (trailing spaces, legacy 'N/S' prefixes). In PayLattice, premium eligibility is driven by shift-pattern code. The production load on 24 Oct used a fresh legacy extract (MD-1023) taken on 23 Oct, which carried these anomalies into production. 18 of the 139 complainants hold flagged records. The rest may carry anomalies that our audit rules do not detect. No change affecting pay calculation was made after parallel-run sign-off (see change log: CR-118 was a label correction). Recommendation: Fenmarch to re-cleanse and reload employee master data before the November run. Under clause 14.3, fixing client-data defects is at Fenmarch's cost.
12	- Ardentra-maintained change log extract, 9–28 Oct, supplied with AR-INC-2291 (change-record): CR-114 | 13 Oct | Bank file header field order corrected | calc impact: none | approved O. Calloway (Payroll Manager).
13	CR-118 | 22 Oct | NSP-02 (night shift premium): display label text correction 'Night Prem' → 'Night Shift Premium' | calc impact: none | test: not required | approved O. Calloway (CAB 21 Oct).
14	REL-7.4 | 24 Oct | PayLattice platform release 7.4, includes the statutory tax table update required from the November pay period | calc impact: platform | vendor regression pack passed.
15	CR-121 | 25 Oct | Payslip header logo replaced | calc impact: none.
16	Note: Ardentra consultants write the entries in this log when a change is requested.
17	- Payroll helpdesk ticket summary, generated 12 Nov; finance bank reconciliation note, 31 Oct (system-record): October pay tickets: 139, from 139 individuals. Every ticket reports an underpayment, and none reports an overpayment. All 139 cite the night shift premium line. No tickets concern basic pay, overtime, tax or deductions. Shortfalls claimed: £37–£201 per person, median £98. By directorate: Operations (treatment works shift teams) 124; Customer Contact overnight team 15. No tickets from staff who work days only. Finance bank reconciliation for the 30 Oct payment: the amounts credited matched the payroll output file for all 2,140 payees.
18	- Email, Malcolm Treharne (Programme Director) to COO, 11 Nov (leadership-account): Ardentra's report makes it clear this is our data. I signed off the cleanse on the strength of the vendor's assurance, and I won't let the November run go wrong for the same reason. My proposal: (1) suspend edit rights for Hannah Lowe's HR data team while the cleanse undergoes a conduct review; (2) re-cleanse and reload the full master data before the 24 Nov calculation; (3) accept the clause 14.3 cost so we don't sour the relationship. Internal audit have asked to look into it, but I don't want to wait for them. Remember that the board brought go-live forward; we can't afford another slip.
19	- Interview notes, Priya Dandekar (payroll officer), 12 Nov, taken by internal audit (staff-account): During the parallel run PD checked the night premium for about 40 night workers. All matched the legacy system 'to the penny'. She says the hours on the October payslips she has looked at agree with the rosters: 'it's the premium amount that's short, not the hours.' She knows a few complainants whose shift codes 'have always been messy', but most of the complainants she knows have clean records. On 23 Oct she asked Ardentra whether CR-118 needed testing and was told by email it was 'cosmetic only'. She thinks Ardentra may have reloaded data at cutover but does not know which extract was used.
20	- Email, Declan Hurst (Operations Manager) to COO, 14 Nov (manager-account): Voluntary night overtime cover across the treatment works has dropped from 88% of requested shifts (Sept–Oct average) to 61% (1–13 Nov). The night teams are angry about the premium and say so. But the new four-on-four-off rota trial also started on 1 Nov for exactly these teams, and staff reps have complained about both. Honestly, I can't tell which one is driving it. Under the agreement with the reps, the rota trial can be paused at one week's notice. I'm under pressure to pause it now.
21	
22	BRIEF:
23	The October shortfalls were caused by a pay-rule change, not by your data. On 22 Oct an Ardentra consultant applied a standard night template to the night premium rule (NSP-02). The change was logged as a "label correction" with no calculation impact. It also moved the premium start from 20:00 to 22:00. The collective agreement, the old rule and Ardentra's own design all say 20:00. The platform's tamper-proof audit trail records the change. Internal audit recalculated pay for all 158 night workers. Shortfalls equal exactly one-third of basic rate for the 20:00–22:00 hours, and the 11 staff who start at 22:00 were paid correctly. Re-running October in Ardentra's test tenant with 20:00 restored matched expected pay for all 158. Data quality flags don't predict who was underpaid, and release 7.4 made no rule changes. Confidence is high.
24	
25	Next steps:
26	- Don't suspend the HR team or pay for a re-cleanse. Don't roll back release 7.4.
27	- Have Ardentra restore the 20:00 start and verify it in test before 24 Nov.
28	- Pay everyone short, including the 8 who didn't complain, in an off-cycle payment.
29	- Dispute the cost under clause 14.3.
30	- Ask Ardentra for the reason the change was recorded as cosmetic.
31	- Keep watching night cover. The rota trial overlaps with the premium issue, so I can't yet separate their effects.
32
